text: dsh-skills-panel 是面向 DSH Web 的技能管理设置面板，通过设置页界面和主机端路由连接技能服务。它可浏览全局及项目技能、搜索 skills.sh 并安装技能、查看 SKILL.md、切换模型自动调用、跟踪来源并检查和更新上游版本，也支持导入现有技能。适合希望在 DSH 网页中集中管理技能的用户。搜索会向 skills.sh 发送查询，搜索结果及技能来源检查会访问 GitHub；可选使用 GITHUB_TOKEN 或 GH_TOKEN 提高 GitHub API 配额。

dsh-skills-panel adds a DSH Web skills page to browse global and project skills, search skills.sh, and install or import skills. It supports viewing SKILL.md, toggling model invocation, tracking sources, and checking or applying updates. Search uses skills.sh and GitHub; GitHub tokens are optional.
想在 DSH 网页里查看和管理全局及项目技能。
有没有办法搜索技能目录并安装到当前项目？
I want to inspect installed skills and check whether their upstream versions have changed.
dsh-skills-panel 的功能「技能浏览与调用开关」：在设置页按全局或项目范围列出技能，并可查看技能正文、切换是否自动注入模型上下文。
dsh-skills-panel 的功能「搜索、安装与更新技能」：在查找页搜索 skills.sh，将技能安装到全局或项目目录，并检查已跟踪来源的更新后按需更新。
dsh-skills-panel 使用前须知：搜索查询发往 skills.sh，来源检查访问 GitHub；可选使用 GITHUB_TOKEN 或 GH_TOKEN。

dsh-skills-panel README · dsh-skills-panel：English | [中文](README.zh.md)

A **Skills** page for the DeepSeek Harness settings dialog: see every skill DSH
can load — global and per project — search and install new ones from
[skills.sh](https://skills.sh), control which skills are auto-injected into the
model context, and get told when an installed skill changes upstream.

> **Unofficial.** This is a third-party plugin. It is not affiliated with or
> endorsed by DeepSeek. It uses only public DSH plugin surfaces.

dsh-skills-panel README · dsh-skills-panel：The page and its entry in the plugin list both follow the language DSH is set
to — English and Chinese — and the plugin list shows its own icon. Both come from
the package's declared [display metadata](#display-metadata).

---

dsh-skills-panel README · What it does：- Lists the effective skill set for a scope, with a source badge per skill
  (`user-dsh`, `project-dsh`, a preset, an agent preset, …) and a marker when a
  project skill overrides a global one of the same name.
- A switch per skill: **on** means the skill stays in the model-visible catalog,
  **off** writes `disable-model-invocation: true` into the skill's frontmatter so
  it drops out of the catalog but stays callable as `/name`. That is DSH's own
  mechanism, not a private convention.
- Skills that are junctions into another tool, or that DSH does not own, are
  shown read-only — the panel will not rewrite a file it shares with someone else.
- **View** expands the skill's SKILL.md inline.
- **Remove** deletes the skill folder, or only the link when the skill is a
  junction (a plain `rmdir` cannot follow a junction into its target).
- **Check all for updates** compares every tracked skill against its repository
  and marks the ones that changed.
- A skill the panel did not install — one copied in, or installed by a script —
  offers **Track source**: tell the panel which repository it came from and it
  takes part in checks and updates like

dsh-skills-panel README · What it does：**Find & install tab**

- Searches skills.sh and gives each result a **GitHub** and a **skills.sh**
  entry point, so you can inspect it yourself before committing.
  The panel downloads nothing on its own: a skill you have not confirmed never
  lands on this machine, not even a byte.
- Results you already have are badged **already installed** and offer
  **Reinstall** instead of **Install**.
- Installs to the global skills root or to the current project (`.dsh/skills`).

**Import tab**

dsh-skills-panel README · What it does：- Brings in a skill folder that already exists on disk, either as a **junction**
  (the original folder stays the source of truth) or as a **copy**.
- Imported skills are deliberately excluded from update checks: they have no
  upstream to compare against.

**Updates**

dsh-skills-panel README · What it does：- **A check downloads nothing.** It asks GitHub for commit ids: one request per
  repository says whether anything in it moved at all, and a skill directory's
  last commit says whether that skill moved. Content is fetched only when you
  install or update.
  On the slow link this was built for, eight repositories went from 26.8 MB and
  about four and a half minutes to roughly 40 KB and a few seconds.
- Once per page load, in the background, every tracked skill is checked. A
  result stands for ten minutes, so reloading the page asks nothing; the panel
  shows how old its answer is.
- **Update** re-checks first and does nothing at all when upstream has not
  moved — including leaving a locally edited copy untouched.
- The auto/manual model-invocation switch is a setting, not content: flipping it
  never shows up as an edit, never manufactures an update, and **survives an
  update** rather than being reset by it.
- If the local copy no longer matches the baseline it was installed with, the
  panel will not replace it silently: it asks first.
- **Track source** is for skills that came from somewhere other than this panel.

dsh-skills-panel README · Install：Requires DSH with the `web` profile and `pnpm` on `PATH`.

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:mathangler/dsh-skills-panel
```

Then restart the web app:

```sh
dsh web
```

`dsh plugin` runs pnpm inside `~/.dsh/profiles/web` and then appends this package
to `dsh.profile.bundles` automatically, because the package declares
`dsh.bundle`. You do not need to edit any YAML.

Open **Settings → Skills**.

dsh-skills-panel README · Update：```sh
dsh plugin --profile web update dsh-skills-panel
```

dsh-skills-panel README · Uninstall：```sh
dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-skills-panel
```

dsh-skills-panel README · How installing a skill works：Installing does **not** use the GitHub REST API, so it needs no token and is not
subject to the 60-requests-per-hour anonymous limit:

dsh-skills-panel README · How installing a skill works：1. The archive is fetched from `codeload.github.com/<repo>/tar.gz/<ref>` — trying
   `HEAD` first, so **no `git` is required**, then `main`, then `master`.
2. `tar` extracts it into a short-lived cache in the system temp directory.
3. The skill directory is located by finding the folder named after the skill id
   that actually contains a `SKILL.md`.
4. `fs.cp` copies it out **whole** — byte for byte, so scripts, images and other
   binary assets come along intact.

dsh-skills-panel README · How installing a skill works：**Installs and updates take that pipeline; a check does not.** Installing is an
action you asked for by name. Searching sends no request for a skill's content,
and a check reads commit ids rather than archives — a stranger's repository
should not appear on your disk before you have decided anything.

dsh-skills-panel README · How installing a skill works：The pipeline needs `codeload.github.com` for content and `api.github.com` for
commit ids, never `raw.githubusercontent.com`. That matters on networks where
`raw` is unreachable while the other two work. If `api.github.com` cannot answer
at all, the check falls back to comparing archives: slower, but still correct.

dsh-skills-panel README · How installing a skill works：Search reads `skills.sh` directly rather than through the `web` capability. That
capability is a deployment choice, and the choice can change what a body *is*: a
profile pointing `fetchProvider` at a service that converts pages to Markdown
gets that service's rendering of a JSON document — every `{ [ : , /` and `"`
escaped — which no JSON parser accepts. Reading a JSON API directly is the same
rule the archive pipeline already follows. The capability is still used as a
fallback, for a deployment whose egress only reaches through it.

dsh-skills-panel README · How installing a skill works：Each tracked skill is recorded in `.skills-panel.json` in its skills root with
its repository, branch, in-repo path, the commit ids the last check compared
against, and two digests of the **whole skill folder** — relative paths plus a
content hash per file, sorted and combined into one value. The manifest is what
makes update checks and clean removals possible; delete it and the panel will
still show the skill, but will not offer updates for it unless you track a source
again.

dsh-skills-panel README · How installing a skill works：`repoHead` and `skillSha` are what the cheap check reads: the repository tip and
the last commit touching the skill's own directory. `upstreamHash` is the same
question answered by content, kept so the archive fallback still works.

dsh-skills-panel README · How installing a skill works：The two digests answer one question each, from separate baselines. `hash` covers
the copy on disk, so **has this copy been edited** — which is why an update asks
before replacing anything. `upstreamHash` covers what the repository published
when that copy was installed, so **has upstream moved**. Only the second decides
the update badge, and only upstream can move it: a switch flip, a hand edit, or a
baseline some other installation rewrote in its own format cannot manufacture an
update, and cannot silence a real one for longer than the check that rebuilt the
baseline.

dsh-skills-panel README · How installing a skill works：A record whose baselines an older version wrote — one that hashed SKILL.md alone,
or that digested the invocation flag — is re-baselined on its first check and
marked `rebased`. The upstream baseline there is taken from the repository, not
from your copy, unless the copy is one this panel installed and nothing has
edited since; reading it off local content whose provenance is unknown is what
turned a local change into a permanent, unapplyable "update available".

dsh-skills-panel README · How installing a skill works：`disable-model-invocation` in SKILL.md is the one thing left out of both digests,
because it is this panel's own switch rather than part of the skill. Counting it
made flipping a switch read as an edit, and a baseline captured through one
disagreed for good with every repository that does not ship the flag: an update
that updating could never clear. The setting is carried across a reinstall
instead, so refreshing a skill no longer resets it.

dsh-skills-panel README · How installing a skill works：Two DSH installations can share one skills root — a desktop app and a `dsh web`
server, say — and then they share this manifest. Each writes its own record in
the same shape, so the two agree; a plugin update only takes effect in a process
that restarts, and until it does, the half still running an older copy reports
its own verdicts from the code it loaded. Those verdicts are now the only thing
it can get wrong: it can no longer move another installation's answer.

dsh-skills-panel README · Display metadata：DSH shows a plugin's title and description in the plugin list from
`locale/<language>.json` in the package:

```json
{ "meta": { "title": "Skills panel", "description": "…" } }
```

dsh-skills-panel README · Display metadata：The file is resolved as `<package>/locale/en.json` **through the package's
`exports` map**, so `"./locale/*.json"` has to be exported and `locale/*.json`
has to be listed in `files` — otherwise the host cannot read it and the list
quietly falls back to the bare package name and the npm `description`. Every
other `.json` beside `en.json` is read as a language, using its filename as the
language id, and the client picks one through the active locale's fallback chain
(`zh-CN` → `zh` → `en`).

dsh-skills-panel README · Display metadata：The icon is `icon.svg` at the package root, declared as `"icon": "./icon.svg"` and
also exported as `"./icon"`. It is drawn on the same 36-unit grid as the shipped
icons, which DSH displays at 36px in a card and 30px in a row, so a different grid
would render at the wrong optical size. DSH inlines it as a base64 data URL,
which is why it references nothing external and carries its own colours rather
than `currentColor`.

dsh-skills-panel README · Display metadata：Every one of those rules is silent when broken: the host falls back to the
package name, the npm `description`, and its own generic artwork. So
`test/plugin-meta.test.mjs` asserts each of them directly, including the
language-id filename pattern, the requirement that English exists, that the
languages actually differ from one another, and that the icon is a real
self-contained drawing on the right grid.

dsh-skills-panel README · Platform notes：- **Windows, macOS and Linux.** There is no shell script and no PowerShell: the
  whole pipeline is Node — `fetch`, `fs.cp`, `fs.symlink`, `fs.rm` — which
  behaves the same on all three. A Windows junction and a POSIX symlink are both
  created with `fs.symlink`, so neither needs elevation.
- **`tar` is the only external tool.** It ships with macOS and Linux, and with
  Windows 10 (1803) and later. You do not need `git`, `curl` or PowerShell. `gh`
  is asked for a token only when the unauthenticated budget runs out, and its
  absence is not an error.
- The update check covers **the whole skill folder**, not just `SKILL.md`, so a
  release that only touches `scripts/` or a bundled asset is still noticed. The
  digest is path-sorted and separator-normalised, so it is identical on all three
  platforms.
- Tests live in `test/` and are not part of the published package: `node
  test/cheap-check.test.mjs` (a check downloads nothing), `node
  test/upstream-baseline.test.mjs` (what the check may and may not answer for),
  `node test/track-source.test.mjs` and `node test/client-load.test.mjs`.
